1.2 Equivalences of categories

We now develop some basic properties of the equivalences introduced in Definition 1.1.4.

1.2.1 Equivalences and lifting

Proposition 1.2.1. Let \(f\colon C\to D\) be a functor. For \(f\) to be an equivalence, it suffices that the following properties hold for every category \(T\):

naive-bijection-isEquiv

Derived · checked against supplied interface

naive-bijection-isEquiv : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  → NaiveBijection f → IsEquiv f
Proof / implementation
naive-bijection-isEquiv {C} {D} {f} b =
  --! begin naive-bijection-inverse-data
  let chosen = NaiveBijection.lift b (id D)
      g = FunctorLift.lift chosen
      ε = FunctorLift.comparison chosen
  --! end naive-bijection-inverse-data
      --! begin naive-bijection-reflection
      η = NaiveBijection.reflect b (g ∘ f) (id C)
        (invIso (comp-unitʳ f) ∙ (comp-unitˡ f ∙ ((ε ▷ f) ∙ invIso (comp-assoc f g f))))
      --! end naive-bijection-reflection
  in record { inverse = g ; sectionIso = invIso η ; retractionIso = invIso ε }

Proof

Proof. Apply the second property to \(\id _D\) to obtain \(g\colon D\to C\) and \(fg\cong \id _D\). The associator, this isomorphism, and the unitors identify \(f(gf)\) with \(f\id _C\). The first property, with \(T=C\), gives \(gf\cong \id _C\). □

Definition 1.2.2 (Section/retraction). Consider a functor \(f\colon C \to D\). A section of \(f\) is a functor \(s\colon D \to C\) equipped with a natural isomorphism \(fs \cong \id _D\). A retraction of \(f\) is a functor \(r\colon D \to C\) equipped with a natural isomorphism \(\id _C \cong rf\).

Lemma 1.2.3. A functor \(f\colon C \to D\) is an equivalence if and only if it admits both a section \(s\) and a retraction \(r\). In this case there exists a natural isomorphism \(s \cong r\) and \(s\) is an inverse of \(f\).

Agda Inverse on both sides implies equivalence

section-retraction-isEquiv

Derived · checked against supplied interface

section-retraction-isEquiv : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  → Section f → Retraction f → IsEquiv f
Proof / implementation
section-retraction-isEquiv {f = f} s r = record
  { inverse = Section.section s
  ; sectionIso = (invIso (section-retraction-iso s r) ▷ f) ∙ Retraction.comparison r
  ; retractionIso = invIso (Section.comparison s) }

section-retraction-iso

Derived · checked against supplied interface

section-retraction-iso : {C D : CAT} {f : MAP C D}
  (s : Section f) (r : Retraction f)
  → NatIso (Section.section s) (Retraction.retraction r)
Proof / implementation
section-retraction-iso {f = f} s r =
  let u = Section.section s
      v = Retraction.retraction r
  in comp-unitʳ v ∙ ((v ◁ Section.comparison s) ∙
     (comp-assoc u f v ∙ ((Retraction.comparison r ▷ u) ∙ invIso (comp-unitˡ u))))

Proof

Proof. If \(f\) is an equivalence with inverse \(g\colon D \to C\), then clearly \(g\) is both a section and a retraction of \(f\). Conversely, given a section \(s\colon D \to C\), \(fs \cong \id _D\) and a retraction \(r\colon D \to C\), \(\id _C \cong rf\), we obtain a natural isomorphism \(s \cong r\) by composing the following chain of natural isomorphisms: \[ s \cong \id _C \circ s \cong (r \circ f) \circ s \cong r \circ (f \circ s) \cong r \circ \id _D \cong r. \]Agda It follows that \(f\) is an equivalence with inverse \(s\), since there are natural isomorphisms \(fs \cong \id _{D}\) and \(sf \cong rf \cong \id _{C}\). □

Agda Inverse on both sides implies equivalence step 1

Agda Composite of equivalences

equiv-compose

Derived · checked against supplied interface

equiv-compose : {C D E : CAT} (f : MAP C D) (g : MAP D E)
  → IsEquiv f → IsEquiv g → IsEquiv (g ∘ f)
Proof / implementation
equiv-compose {C} {D} {E} f g ef eg =
  let u : MAP D C
      u = IsEquiv.inverse ef
      v : MAP E D
      v = IsEquiv.inverse eg
      --! begin equiv-compose-left
      left : NatIso ((u ∘ v) ∘ (g ∘ f)) (id C)
      left = invIso (IsEquiv.sectionIso ef) ∙
        ((u ◁ comp-unitˡ f) ∙ ((u ◁ (invIso (IsEquiv.sectionIso eg) ▷ f)) ∙
        ((u ◁ invIso (comp-assoc f g v)) ∙ comp-assoc (g ∘ f) v u)))
      --! end equiv-compose-left
      --! begin equiv-compose-right
      right : NatIso ((g ∘ f) ∘ (u ∘ v)) (id E)
      right = invIso (IsEquiv.retractionIso eg) ∙
        ((g ◁ comp-unitˡ v) ∙ ((g ◁ (invIso (IsEquiv.retractionIso ef) ▷ v)) ∙
        ((g ◁ invIso (comp-assoc v u f)) ∙ comp-assoc (u ∘ v) f g)))
      --! end equiv-compose-right
  in record { inverse = u ∘ v ; sectionIso = invIso left ; retractionIso = invIso right }

Proof

Proof. If \(g\) and \(f\) are equivalences, then so is \(gf\) by Lemma 1.2.5. If \(f\) and \(gf\) are equivalences, then we may rewrite \(g\) as the composite \(g \cong g \circ \id _{D} \cong g \circ f \circ f^{-1} \cong gf \circ f^{-1}\), so that \(g\) is the composite of two equivalences and hence itself an equivalence. A similar argument shows that \(f\) is an equivalence whenever \(g\) and \(gf\) are equivalences. □

Proof

Proof. Consider the functors \(f' := f \circ (gf)^{-1}\colon E \to D\) and \(h' := (hg)^{-1} \circ h \colon E \to D\). Then there are natural isomorphisms \[ g \circ f' \cong g \circ f \circ (gf)^{-1} \cong gf \circ (gf)^{-1} \cong \id _{E} \]Agda and \[ h' \circ g \cong (hg)^{-1} \circ h \circ g \cong (hg)^{-1} \circ hg \cong \id _{D}. \]Agda Hence it follows from Lemma 1.2.3 that \(g\) is an equivalence. In light of Lemma 1.2.7, we then get that also \(f\) and \(h\) are equivalences, and then so is \(hgf\). □

Definition 1.2.9. We say that a functor \(f\colon C \to D\) is a retract of a functor \(f'\colon C' \to D'\) if there exists a commutative diagram of the form

Agda Retract

RetractDiagram

Definition · checked

record RetractDiagram {C D C′ D′ : CAT} (f : MAP C D) (f′ : MAP C′ D′) : Set m where
  field
    g : MAP C C′
    h : MAP C′ C
    k : MAP D D′
    j : MAP D′ D
    leftSquare : NatIso (f′ ∘ g) (k ∘ f)
    rightSquare : NatIso (f ∘ h) (j ∘ f′)
    α : NatIso (id C) (h ∘ g)
    β : NatIso (j ∘ k) (id D)

  loop : NatIso f f
  loop = comp-unitˡ f ∙ ((β ▷ f) ∙
    (invIso (comp-assoc f k j) ∙ ((j ◁ leftSquare) ∙
    (comp-assoc g f′ j ∙ ((rightSquare ▷ g) ∙
    (invIso (comp-assoc g h f) ∙ ((f ◁ α) ∙ invIso (comp-unitʳ f))))))))

Lemma 1.2.10. Assume that \(f\colon C \to D\) is a retract of \(f'\colon C' \to D'\). If \(f'\) is an equivalence, then so is \(f\).

Agda Equivalences closed under retracts

retract-isEquiv

Derived · checked against supplied interface

retract-isEquiv : {C D C′ D′ : CAT} {f : MAP C D} {f′ : MAP C′ D′}
  → Retract f f′ → IsEquiv f′ → IsEquiv f
Proof / implementation
retract-isEquiv {f = f} {f′} R e =
  let open RetractDiagram (Retract.diagram R)
      u = IsEquiv.inverse e
      --! begin retract-inverse
      w = h ∘ (u ∘ k)
      --! end retract-inverse
      --! begin retract-counit
      counit = β ∙ ((j ◁ comp-unitˡ k) ∙
        ((j ◁ (invIso (IsEquiv.retractionIso e) ▷ k)) ∙
        ((j ◁ invIso (comp-assoc k u f′)) ∙
        (comp-assoc (u ∘ k) f′ j ∙ ((rightSquare ▷ (u ∘ k)) ∙
        invIso (comp-assoc (u ∘ k) h f))))))
      --! end retract-counit
      --! begin retract-inverse-unit
      inverseUnit = invIso α ∙ ((h ◁ comp-unitˡ g) ∙
        ((h ◁ (invIso (IsEquiv.sectionIso e) ▷ g)) ∙
        ((h ◁ invIso (comp-assoc g f′ u)) ∙
        ((h ◁ (u ◁ invIso leftSquare)) ∙
        ((h ◁ comp-assoc f k u) ∙ comp-assoc f (u ∘ k) h)))))
      --! end retract-inverse-unit
  in record { inverse = w ; sectionIso = invIso inverseUnit ; retractionIso = invIso counit }

Proof

Proof. Let \((f')^{-1}\colon D' \to C'\) be an inverse of \(f'\). We claim that the composite \(w := h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k\colon D \to C\) is inverse to \(f\). Indeed, we have natural isomorphisms \[ f \circ w \cong f \circ h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k \cong j \circ f' \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k \cong j \circ k \cong \id _{D} \]Agda and \[ w \circ f \cong h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ k \circ f \cong h \circ (f')^{-1} \circ f' \circ g \cong h \circ g \cong \id _{C}. \]Agda This finishes the proof. □

retract-isEquiv {f = f} {f′} R e =
  let open RetractDiagram (Retract.diagram R)
      u = IsEquiv.inverse e
      --! begin retract-inverse
      w = h ∘ (u ∘ k)
      --! end retract-inverse
      --! begin retract-counit

        ((j ◁ invIso (comp-assoc k u f′)) ∙
        (comp-assoc (u ∘ k) f′ j ∙ ((rightSquare ▷ (u ∘ k)) ∙
        invIso (comp-assoc (u ∘ k) h f))))))
      --! end retract-counit

        ((h ◁ (invIso (IsEquiv.sectionIso e) ▷ g)) ∙
        ((h ◁ invIso (comp-assoc g f′ u)) ∙
        ((h ◁ (u ◁ invIso leftSquare)) ∙
        ((h ◁ comp-assoc f k u) ∙ comp-assoc f (u ∘ k) h)))))
      --! end retract-inverse-unit
  in record { inverse = w ; sectionIso = invIso inverseUnit ; retractionIso = invIso counit }

postWhisker-isEquiv

Derived · checked against supplied interface

postWhisker-isEquiv : {B C D : CAT} (F : MAP C D) → IsEquiv F
  → (f g : MAP B C) → IsEquiv (postWhisker {f = f} {g} F)
Proof / implementation
postWhisker-isEquiv F e f g =
  let G = IsEquiv.inverse e
      first = post-composite f g F G
        (post-change (invIso (IsEquiv.sectionIso e)) f g (post-id f g))
      second = post-composite (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g) G F
        (post-change (invIso (IsEquiv.retractionIso e)) (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)
          (post-id (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)))
  in TwoOutOfSix.first (two-out-of-six (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G)
       (postWhisker F) first second)

Let \(F\colon C\to D\) have inverse \(G\), and let \(a,b\colon T\to C\). Consider \[ (a\cong b)\xrightarrow {F\star -}(Fa\cong Fb) \xrightarrow {G\star -}(GFa\cong GFb) \xrightarrow {F\star -}(FGFa\cong FGFb). \] Interchange with \(GF\cong \id _C\) identifies the composite of the first two functors with transport along its endpoint isomorphisms. Hence that composite is an equivalence. The composite of the last two is an equivalence for the same reason, using \(FG\cong \id _D\). The 2-out-of-6 property proves the claim. Prewhiskering is treated in the same way. □

post-change {F = F} {G} τ f g = square-left (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G)
  (τ ▷ f) (τ ▷ g)

   (interchange-fixedOuter F G f g τ ∙
    invIso (isoComp-cong (idIso _) (comp-unitʳ (postWhisker F)))))

Agda Whiskering by equivalence step 3

postWhisker-isEquiv

Derived · checked against supplied interface

postWhisker-isEquiv : {B C D : CAT} (F : MAP C D) → IsEquiv F
  → (f g : MAP B C) → IsEquiv (postWhisker {f = f} {g} F)
Proof / implementation
postWhisker-isEquiv F e f g =
  let G = IsEquiv.inverse e
      first = post-composite f g F G
        (post-change (invIso (IsEquiv.sectionIso e)) f g (post-id f g))
      second = post-composite (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g) G F
        (post-change (invIso (IsEquiv.retractionIso e)) (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)
          (post-id (F ∘ f) (F ∘ g)))
  in TwoOutOfSix.first (two-out-of-six (postWhisker F) (postWhisker G)
       (postWhisker F) first second)

two-out-of-six

Derived · checked against supplied interface

two-out-of-six : {C D E F : CAT}
  (f : MAP C D) (g : MAP D E) (h : MAP E F)
  → IsEquiv (g ∘ f) → IsEquiv (h ∘ g) → TwoOutOfSix f g h
Proof / implementation
two-out-of-six f g h egf ehg =
  --! begin two-out-of-six-inverses
  let u = IsEquiv.inverse egf
      v = IsEquiv.inverse ehg
  --! end two-out-of-six-inverses
      --! begin two-out-of-six-section
      s = record { section = f ∘ u
                 ; comparison = invIso (IsEquiv.retractionIso egf) ∙ invIso (comp-assoc u f g) }
      --! end two-out-of-six-section
      --! begin two-out-of-six-retraction
      r = record { retraction = v ∘ h
                 ; comparison = invIso (comp-assoc g h v) ∙ IsEquiv.sectionIso ehg }
      --! end two-out-of-six-retraction
      --! begin two-out-of-six-middle
      eg = section-retraction-isEquiv s r
      --! end two-out-of-six-middle
      --! begin two-out-of-six-conclusion
      ef = equiv-cancel-left f g eg egf
      eh = equiv-cancel-right g h eg ehg
  in record { first = ef ; middle = eg ; last = eh
            ; composite = equiv-compose (g ∘ f) h egf eh }
      --! end two-out-of-six-conclusion

Corollary 1.2.12 (Lifting through equivalences). Prewhiskering or postwhiskering by an equivalence lifts a specified natural isomorphism, together with an identification of its image with that isomorphism. It also lifts and reflects identifications between natural isomorphisms.

equiv-reflect : {C D X : CAT} {f : MAP C D} (e : IsEquiv f)
  (u v : MAP X C) → NatIso (f ∘ u) (f ∘ v) → NatIso u v
Proof / implementation

  let g = IsEquiv.inverse e

Proof

Proof. Apply an inverse of the equivalence of isomorphism animae from Lemma 1.2.11, and apply the same lemma to that equivalence for the assertion about identifications. □

1.2.2 Products and their comparisons

Remark 1.2.13. Given categories \(C\) and \(D\), a span from \(C\) to \(D\) is a triple \((T,f,g)\) consisting of functors \(f\colon T\to C\) and \(g\colon T\to D\). Axiom A.3 makes \((C\times D,\pr _1,\pr _2)\) the terminal span: there is a map \((f,g)\colon T\to C\times D\) with specified comparisons on both legs, and any two such maps are naturally isomorphic compatibly with those comparisons. Indeed, lift the two leg comparisons through Equation (1.1); its higher lifting property supplies the corresponding identifications between comparisons.

Proof

Proof. We need to provide natural isomorphisms \((\pr _2,\pr _1) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) \cong \id _{C \times D}\) and \((\pr _2,\pr _1) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) \cong \id _{D \times C}\). By symmetry, it will suffice to produce the first natural isomorphism. For this, it will in turn suffice to produce natural isomorphisms after composing with the functors \(\pr _1\) and \(\pr _2\). For the composition with \(\pr _1\) we compute that \[ \pr _1 \circ ((\pr _2,\pr _1) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1)) \cong (\pr _1 \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1)) \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) \cong \pr _2 \circ (\pr _2,\pr _1) \cong \pr _1, \] which is indeed isomorphic to \(\pr _1 \circ \id _{C \times D}\). The case for composition with \(\pr _2\) is analogous. This finishes the proof. □

Proof

Proof. The composite \(\pr _1 \circ (\id _{C}, p_{C})\colon C \to C\) is isomorphic to \(\id _{C}\) by the defining property of \((\id _{C}, p_{C})\). To show that the composite \((\id _{C}, p_{C}) \circ \pr _1\colon C \times * \to C \times *\) is isomorphic to \(\id _{C \times *}\), it will suffice to do so after composing with \(\pr _1\) and with \(\pr _2\). The case for \(\pr _2\) is clear, since any two functors \(C \times * \to *\) are isomorphic. In the case of \(\pr _1\) we compute \[ \pr _1 \circ ((\id _{C}, p_{C}) \circ \pr _1) \cong (\pr _1 \circ (\id _{C}, p_{C})) \circ \pr _1 \cong \id _{C} \circ \pr _1 \cong \pr _1 \cong \pr _1 \circ \id _{C \times *}, \] where the first isomorphism is associativity, the second is the relation proved in the first paragraph, and the third and fourth are unitality. This finishes the proof. □

pairing-absolute : {X C D : CAT} {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D}
  (α : NatIso f f′) (β : NatIso g g′) → Iso₂ (pairing α β) (pair-cong α β)

pairing-absolute {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} α β =
  let first = isoComp-cong (const-One (invIso (pair-β₁ f′ g′)))

      back = IsEquiv.inverse (product-isoMap-isEquiv (pair f g) (pair f′ g′))
  in back ◁ pair-cong first second

Derived · checked against supplied interface

family-pair-pre-full : {A R X C D : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D} {r s : MAP R X}
  (α : MAP A (f ≅ f′)) (β : MAP A (g ≅ g′)) (γ : MAP A (r ≅ s))
  → NatIso (pairing (α ⋆ γ) (β ⋆ γ) ∙ const (pair-pre f g r))
      (const (pair-pre f′ g′ s) ∙ (pairing α β ⋆ γ))
Proof / implementation
family-pair-pre-full {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} {r} {s} α β γ =
  let outer = pairing (α ▷ s) (β ▷ s)
      inner = pairing (f ◁ γ) (g ◁ γ)
      before = const (pair-pre f g r)
      middle = const (pair-pre f g s)
      after = const (pair-pre f′ g′ s)
      input = pairing α β ▷ s
      substitution = pair f g ◁ γ
  in assoc after input substitution ∙
    (isoComp-cong (family-pair-pre-inputs α β s) (idIso substitution) ∙
      (invIso (assoc outer middle substitution) ∙
        (isoComp-cong (idIso outer) (family-pair-pre-substitution f g γ) ∙
          (assoc outer inner before ∙
            isoComp-cong (pairing-composition (α ▷ s) (f ◁ γ) (β ▷ s) (g ◁ γ))
              (idIso before)))))

      output = pairIsoMap (f ∘ pr₁) (f′ ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂) (g′ ∘ pr₂)
      point = pair α β
      first = (preWhisker pr₁ ◁ pair-β₁ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₁ (preWhisker pr₁)
      second = (preWhisker pr₂ ◁ pair-β₂ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₂ (preWhisker pr₂)
  in pairIsoMap-at (α ▷ pr₁) (β ▷ pr₂) ∙
    ((output ◁ (pair-cong first second ∙
      pair-pre (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂) point)) ∙
      comp-assoc point input output)

family-pair-pre-full : {A R X C D : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP X C} {g g′ : MAP X D} {r s : MAP R X}
  (α : MAP A (f ≅ f′)) (β : MAP A (g ≅ g′)) (γ : MAP A (r ≅ s))
  → NatIso (pairing (α ⋆ γ) (β ⋆ γ) ∙ const (pair-pre f g r))
      (const (pair-pre f′ g′ s) ∙ (pairing α β ⋆ γ))
Proof / implementation
family-pair-pre-full {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} {r} {s} α β γ =
  let outer = pairing (α ▷ s) (β ▷ s)
      inner = pairing (f ◁ γ) (g ◁ γ)
      before = const (pair-pre f g r)
      middle = const (pair-pre f g s)
      after = const (pair-pre f′ g′ s)
      input = pairing α β ▷ s
      substitution = pair f g ◁ γ
  in assoc after input substitution ∙
    (isoComp-cong (family-pair-pre-inputs α β s) (idIso substitution) ∙
      (invIso (assoc outer middle substitution) ∙
        (isoComp-cong (idIso outer) (family-pair-pre-substitution f g γ) ∙
          (assoc outer inner before ∙
            isoComp-cong (pairing-composition (α ▷ s) (f ◁ γ) (β ▷ s) (g ◁ γ))
              (idIso before)))))

      b = pair-β₁ (f ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂)

productIsoMap-at

Derived · checked against supplied interface

productIsoMap-at : {C C′ D D′ : CAT}
  {f f′ : MAP C C′} {g g′ : MAP D D′}
  (α : NatIso f f′) (β : NatIso g g′)
  → Iso₂ (productIsoMap f f′ g g′ ∘ pair α β) (productMap-cong α β)
Proof / implementation
productIsoMap-at {f = f} {f′} {g} {g′} α β =
  let input = pair (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂)
      output = pairIsoMap (f ∘ pr₁) (f′ ∘ pr₁) (g ∘ pr₂) (g′ ∘ pr₂)
      point = pair α β
      first = (preWhisker pr₁ ◁ pair-β₁ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₁ (preWhisker pr₁)
      second = (preWhisker pr₂ ◁ pair-β₂ α β) ∙ comp-assoc point pr₂ (preWhisker pr₂)
  in pairIsoMap-at (α ▷ pr₁) (β ▷ pr₂) ∙
    ((output ◁ (pair-cong first second ∙
      pair-pre (preWhisker pr₁ ∘ pr₁) (preWhisker pr₂ ∘ pr₂) point)) ∙
      comp-assoc point input output)

Proof

Proof. For each \(h,k\colon T\to C\times D\), use an inverse of the equivalence \[ (h\cong k)\iso (\pr _1 h\cong \pr _1 k)\times (\pr _2 h\cong \pr _2 k). \] Pairing the component comparisons gives the comparison for products. Its projections come equipped with identifications with those components. For identity and composition, the two projected pastings are identified by the whiskering laws. For iterated precomposition, they are identified by the primitive pentagon and triangle. Lift these identifications through the displayed equivalence using Corollary 1.2.12. Their action on identifications is the action of these functors on natural isomorphisms, obtained by whiskering. □

Proof / implementation
pair-pre-id {X} f g =
